record.summary: Bright Path Logistics, a small trucking firm, is being sued by Orion Traders for ₹1,800,000 alleging breach of a supply and transport agreement dated 1 February. The owner, Anil Chopra, denies signing the contract, noting differences in the signature and inconsistencies in the document. He acknowledges email discussions and a brief meeting in January about a possible trial arrangement, but says no contract was finalized. Orion claims Anil signed in person and that performance began when Bright Path moved three loads in March, which Anil says were separate one‑off jobs. He wants to know if the contract can be challenged as forged, how to prove it, and whether he remains liable despite the disputed signature.
record.goal: To challenge the validity of the alleged contract and avoid liability for the claimed breach.
questions: What are the exact dates (or approximate dates) of the email exchanges and the meeting with Orion’s representative in January?
On which dates in March were the three loads transported and the corresponding invoices issued?
Do you have the original hard‑copy of the signed contract, or only the scanned PDF?
Have you obtained any handwriting comparison or forensic analysis of the signature on the contract versus your known signatures?
Where is Bright Path Logistics located and where did the alleged performance (the three loads) take place?
contradictions: The contract shows a signing date of 1 February but an “effective from” date of 1 March, which is after the signing date.
Clause 14 refers to a company registration number that Bright Path only received on 20 February, after the alleged signing date.
The signature on the contract differs in loop style from Anil’s known signatures on his licence and bank forms.
Metadata of the scanned PDF indicates the file was created after the alleged signing date.
Orion claims performance began when Bright Path moved three loads in March, while Anil says those were separate one‑off jobs not covered by any contract.
evidence: Contract copy shows inconsistent fonts between pages 1‑9 and pages 10‑12, and the signature page has a different margin and paper tone.
Date next to signature is 1 February, but the “effective from” clause on page 2 states 1 March.
Clause 14 refers to a company registration number Bright Path received only on 20 February.
Anil’s signatures on his driving licence and bank forms show a visibly different loop in the capital “A.”
Emails from January show negotiation of rates but no final contract; last email says “will send draft for review.”
Three invoices from March for freight, paid by Orion, reference one‑off jobs without citing the agreement.
Scanned PDF of the contract; file metadata indicates creation after the alleged signing date.

suggestions.title: Original records and an evidence log
suggestions.look_for: Keep records you lawfully have, with their surrounding context. For each item note the related event, who provided it, when you received it, and any transfer.
suggestions.why: The log distinguishes what you observed from what someone later told you and makes it easier to check the source.
suggestions.action: Keep an unchanged original and label working copies. Avoid editing originals, guessing gaps, or sharing evidence publicly.
